t:
(a) Authorization of Appropriations.—Funds are hereby authorized to be appropriated to the Department of Energy for fiscal year 2017 for the activities of the National Nuclear Security Administration in carrying out programs as specified in the funding table in section 4701. 
    (b) Authorization of New Plant Projects.—From funds referred to in subsection (a) that are available for carrying out plant projects, the Secretary of Energy may carry out new plant projects for the National Nuclear Security Administration as follows:  Project 17–D–630, Expand Electrical Distribution System, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Livermore, California, $25,000,000.  Project 17–D–640, U1a Complex Enhancements Project, Nevada National Security Site, Mercury, Nevada, $11,500,000.  Project 17–D–911, BL Fire System Upgrade, Bettis Atomic Power Laboratory, West Mifflin, Pennsylvania, $1,400,000.

fable.w: This section only authorizes appropriations and lets the Secretary of Energy carry out named plant projects. It contains no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. The tempting reading is that authority to carry out projects at specific local sites implies outside involvement, but every actor named is federal and no participatory process is prescribed.
fable.s: Funds are hereby authorized to be appropriated to the Department of Energy for fiscal year 2017 for the activities of the National Nuclear Security Administration

opus.w: This section only authorizes appropriations for the National Nuclear Security Administration and lets the Secretary of Energy carry out three named plant projects. It names state locations (California, Nevada, Pennsylvania), which might look like it involves outsiders. But those are just project sites. Nothing requires consulting states, local governments, experts, or the public. There is also no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes appropriations and lists specific construction projects for the National Nuclear Security Administration. It grants the Secretary of Energy the authority to carry out these projects but does not require or recommend consultation with any parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the public). All actors mentioned are federal officials or agencies.
qwen_chat.s: From funds referred to in subsection (a) that are available for carrying out plant projects, the Secretary of Energy may carry out new plant projects for the National Nuclear Security Administration as follows:
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Secretary of Energy "may carry out" projects, this implies a decision-making process that could involve outside input. However, the text itself only authorizes funding and lists specific projects; it does not mandate or describe any consultation with non-federal entities (like states, tribes, or the public) before these decisions are made. The actors involved are entirely within the federal government (Department of Energy, Secretary of Energy).
